triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue clearly reports a bug in CLI version 0.43.0 where standard built-in tools (such as activate_skill, google_web_search, and web_fetch) are missing from the tools list, leaving only ReadFile, Shell, and WriteFile. Complete client environment details and expected vs actual behavior are provided.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: The issue is caused by tool registration filtering logic in packages/core/src/config/config.ts when processing core tools or tool allowlists. Fixing the tool matching and registration logic in config.ts is a localized bug fix in a single configuration file.

summary.problem: In CLI version 0.43.0, built-in tools such as activate_skill, google_web_search, and web_fetch are missing from the available tools list, leaving only ReadFile, Shell, and WriteFile registered.
summary.root_cause: The maybeRegister helper in packages/core/src/config/config.ts filters registered tools against the coreTools allowlist using toolName and className. When coreTools filtering is active or when tool identifier resolution mismatches occur between internal tool names (e.g., activate_skill) and class names (e.g., ActivateSkillTool), non-file/shell tools are inadvertently omitted during createToolRegistry().
summary.context: Tool registration in createToolRegistry() uses maybeRegister to conditionally instantiate tools based on this.getCoreTools(). Mismatches in tool identifier resolution cause tools like ActivateSkillTool and WebSearchTool to be filtered out.

steps: Inspect maybeRegister in packages/core/src/config/config.ts to ensure coreTools filtering checks both canonical tool IDs (e.g., ActivateSkillTool.Name) and class names properly.
Ensure ActivateSkillTool and other default core tools are correctly registered when coreTools is undefined or when skill tools should be implicitly enabled.
Verify that tool allowlist matching in maybeRegister correctly resolves both snake_case tool names (e.g., activate_skill) and PascalCase class names (e.g., ActivateSkillTool).

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: When creating a ToolRegistry under default configuration, all standard built-in tools including activate_skill, google_web_search, and web_fetch are registered and available.
verification_steps: Add a unit test in packages/core/src/config/config.test.ts verifying that createToolRegistry() registers ActivateSkillTool, WebSearchTool, and WebFetchTool alongside file and shell tools under default configuration.
Run npm test packages/core/src/config/config.test.ts using Vitest to verify all tool registration tests pass.
